newsitem.title: JAPAN: Citizen Watch sees 96/97 profits up from forecast.
newsitem.headline: Citizen Watch sees 96/97 profits up from forecast.

text.p: Citizen Watch Co Ltd said on Friday that it expects parent current profits in the fiscal year ending on March 31, 1997, to be more than 10 percent larger than its earlier forecast of 11 billion yen.
He added that Citizen would see further profit growth in 1997/98.
The expected rise was not only because of the yen's fall, Nakajima said, although 75 percent of sales comes from exports.
This is because about 90 percent of its exports are yen-denominated and also because the company has been implementing cost-cutting efforts to cope with the yen's rise in the past.
Compared with the past, the impact of movements in foreign exchange markets on the company have diminished, he said. He said he wanted the dollar to stay around 110 yen.
"I don't want the dollar to move drastically on either side. It would be better if it stays around 110 yen," Nakajima said.
He said the rise in the consumption tax would have a limited impact on Citizen's business because the firm exports 70 to 80 percent of its watches.
Nakajima said he thought Citizen would need to improve its return on earnings, but did not elaborate.
Generally speaking, Japanese companies are often criticised for their low return on earnings.
On Citizen's overseas business, he said the firm could not expect profits from its business in China for the time being.
He said Citizen expects its business to be solid in the United States, Europe, Latin America and the Middle East this year.
